scope.updateModel: Fully dynamic: edge insertions and deletions
scope.output: A continuously maintained scalar estimate ν of the optimum matching size
scope.ratioDefinition: β·OPT ≤ ν ≤ OPT; larger β is better; a source using approximation factor α≥1 is plotted as β=1/α
scope.adversary: Adaptive update sequences for all principal rows
scope.quantifiers: Every accuracy-family endpoint is a limit as ε tends to zero. Each time bound holds for its stated ε; polylogarithmic means every fixed positive ε. m denotes the current number of edges.
scope.query: O(1) to read the maintained scalar. Reporting matching edges or answering an implicit mate query is a different output operation.
scope.exclusions: Weighted, bipartite-only, incremental-only, decremental-only, and graph-streaming results are outside this scope.

coverage: Seven principal algorithm milestones, plus a symbolic reduction. This is a scoped primary-source review, not an exhaustive catalogue of every parameter or graph-class variant. No verified impossibility threshold for constant-factor approximation is asserted.

results.title: Fully Dynamic (1+ε)-Approximate Matchings
results.output: size of an explicitly maintained matching
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 1.1; ε-dependence in the abstract and Section 3; worst-case conversion in Appendix A.3
results.statement: An explicit matching within a factor 1+ε of optimum can be maintained in general graphs. Its edge count provides the same approximation to the matching size.
results.notes: The dot at 1 is a limiting endpoint as ε approaches zero. The theorem does not maintain an exact maximum matching at this update cost. Here m is the current number of graph edges.
results.queryTime: O(1) to read the maintained size
results.queryDerivation: Reading a continuously maintained scalar, or the counter of a maintained explicit matching, takes constant time; this is not a claim about returning all matching edges.

results.title: Deterministic Dynamic Matching in Worst-Case Update Time
results.output: size of an explicitly maintained matching
results.parameterRange: Every fixed ε > 0; Oε hides polynomial dependence on 1/ε
results.statement: A deterministic algorithm maintains an explicit (2+ε)-approximate matching with polylogarithmic worst-case update time. Counting its edges yields a size estimate with β=1/(2+ε).
results.notes: This is a historical deterministic baseline; later randomized size estimators give a higher guaranteed fraction. Deterministic correctness also covers adaptive update sequences.
results.queryTime: O(1) to read the maintained size
results.queryDerivation: Reading a continuously maintained scalar, or the counter of a maintained explicit matching, takes constant time; this is not a claim about returning all matching edges.

results.notes: Theorem 2 additionally replaces m¹ᐟ⁴ by √a when graph arboricity is bounded by a. That sparsity parameter is a separate refinement; the row uses the unrestricted general-graph theorem.

results.notes: Independent of the concurrent Bhattacharya–Kiss–Saranurak–Wajc result. This general-graph row is distinct from the stronger guarantees for bipartite graphs elsewhere in the same paper.

results.probability: approximation and update bound hold with high probability
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 1.1, printed p. 2; Proposition 2.1 for continuous size maintenance
results.statement: The general-graph estimator achieves α=1.973+ε, or β=1/(1.973+ε), with a polylogarithmic worst-case update bound robust to adaptive updates.
results.notes: The limiting fraction is about 0.50684. The paper’s better bipartite factor 1+1/√2+ε is not used for this general-graph row.

results.authors: Sayan Bhattacharya, Peter Kiss & Thatchaphol Saranurak
results.shortTitle: Near-optimal size in truly sublinear time
results.title: Dynamic (1+ε)-Approximate Matching Size in Truly Sublinear Update Time
results.output: matching-size estimate; optional implicit matching queries
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 1.2, printed p. 2; dynamic conversion in Section 7
results.parameterRange: Every fixed ε > 0; the positive exponent saving depends on ε
results.statement: A near-optimal matching-size estimate can be maintained with a polynomial improvement over √m update time, with high probability against adaptive updates.
results.notes: No numerical exponent is inferred from Ωε(1). The paper also offers an implicit mate query for a vertex in m^{1/2+f(ε)} time, where f(ε) tends to zero with ε; that query does not explicitly maintain the edge set. The endpoint 1 denotes a family of approximations, not exact size.
results.queryTime: O(1) to read the maintained size
results.queryDerivation: Reading a continuously maintained scalar, or the counter of a maintained explicit matching, takes constant time; this is not a claim about returning all matching edges.

results.authors: Amir Azarmehr, Soheil Behnezhad & Mohammad Roghani
results.title: Fully Dynamic Matching: (2−√2)-Approximation in Polylog Update Time
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 3, printed p. 10; Proposition 5.1 and proof of Theorem 3 on printed p. 22
results.statement: For every fixed ε, the maintained estimate guarantees a fraction 2−√2−ε of optimum in general graphs, with polylogarithmic worst-case update time against adaptive updates.
results.notes: The best verified polylogarithmic quality in this review approaches 0.585786. This point is not a lower bound or a proved barrier. Dependence on accuracy is exponential in a polynomial of 1/ε, so the fixed-ε qualifier matters.
results.queryTime: O(1) to read the maintained size
results.queryDerivation: Reading a continuously maintained scalar, or the counter of a maintained explicit matching, takes constant time; this is not a claim about returning all matching edges.

relatedResults.statement: For each fixed α>3/2, an α-approximate explicit matching algorithm with update cost tu yields a strictly better constant approximation for its size at only polylogarithmic overhead.
relatedResults.notes: The reduction preserves adaptive robustness and worst-case update bounds when the input algorithm has them. Its hidden constant is not turned into a numeric dot. relatedResults.title: Unifying and Strengthening Hardness for Dynamic Problems via the Online Matrix-Vector Multiplication Conjecture
relatedResults.updateTime: No simultaneous m^{1/2−δ} updates and m^{1−δ} queries
relatedResults.sourceLocation: Corollary 3.4 and following reductions; Table 5 footnote
relatedResults.statement: Under the OMv conjecture, polynomial preprocessing cannot coexist with update time m^{1/2-delta} and query time m^{1-delta} for fixed delta>0 for exact bipartite perfect matching or exact maximum-matching size. The fully dynamic lower bound allows amortized updates; the corresponding partially dynamic statement is worst-case.
relatedResults.summary: Applies to exact matching size or perfect-matching detection. It does not rule out the constant-factor approximations above.
relatedResults.notes: At dense m=Theta(n^2), this excludes truly sublinear-in-n updates when queries are sufficiently fast. The reduction distinguishes exact matching sizes; it is not a constant-factor approximation lower bound.

relatedResults.statement: For bipartite graphs, the maintained size estimate exceeds a two-thirds approximation by an absolute positive constant, with the displayed worst-case update bound against adaptive updates.
relatedResults.notes: The reference slide calls this B’22 using its preprint year; publication was SODA 2023. This theorem does not hold for arbitrary general graphs as stated. Any plotted horizontal position should be labeled symbolically as 2/3+δ₀ rather than interpreted as an exact numerical ratio.
